reviews.reasons: No plan with a cheap test is the right posture, and the $62 test fits the $250 risk cap, but the test's proof does not decide the goal and the funding path it leads to breaks the cap. Recomputed: per build $1,500 - $600 designer (unquoted) - ~$43.80 Stripe on two charges = ~$856; 4 builds = ~$3,425, minus $62 = ~$3,363 >= $3,000, so 4 completed and paid builds are needed inside 21 days. The designers must be paid before or during the 7-day build, but deposits taken around day 7 are not usable until Stripe's first payout (7-14 days, i.e. day 14-21). Paying four designers from the owner's pocket would put up to $2,400 at risk against a $250 cap; paying them only from settled deposits pushes builds to day 21-28 and the balances past day 21. The resolution must say how designer fees are funded inside $250 (e.g. designer paid on delivery, or at most one build advanced) and make that a stop condition. The proof (2 deposits) is also not sized to the 4 builds the target needs, and the second 1,000-email batch 'at no added cost' conflicts with the Growth plan's 1,000 uploaded-contact limit cited in the same research.
findings: Exposure: max owner advance with four $600 builds before payout = $2,400 >> $250 cap; the plan's trace shows only the $62 test, so the follow-on is not shown to fit.

Timeline: deposit day ~7 + first payout up to 14 days = day 21 usable; + 7-day build = day 28. Only the 7-day best-case payout leaves a path; the proof should require it (Stripe account already paying out) rather than read it on day 7.
Proof sizing: require deposits/replies consistent with 4 paid builds by ~day 10, not 2; stop otherwise.

Price: $1,500 is near the top of the verified Thumbtack range ($614-$1,817, avg $1,057); the named pros' $1,500-$2,500 rates were rejected at the evidence gate and should not be cited as evidence. A market range is not what these cold-emailed buyers are shown paying - the deposits measure it.
Deliverability: a fresh sending domain bought on day 0 usually needs warm-up before 1,000 cold sends; unevidenced either way, but it threatens the day-7 read.
Exclusions of resume, chatbot and Fiverr routes are reasoned correctly (sales counts, unreadable budgets, 14-day clearance).

noPlan.decisiveGap: No evidence that any US local-service business reached by cold email will pay a $1,500 website deposit within the first week: CURRENT_DEMAND has no buying signal and CONVERSION has no measured close rate. Paying designers before Stripe's first payout would breach the $250 risk cap, so only orders paid in full by about day 10, built by a designer paid on delivery, can settle by day 21.
noPlan.resolution: Spend $122 (Instantly Hypergrowth $107 for 25,000 contacts + one $15 domain), the only owner money at risk, plus 11 owner hours: email 2,000 local-service businesses days 2-10 offering the $1,500 site paid in full up front, and get 3 fixed designer quotes for 7-day delivery paid on delivery (so no designer fee is ever advanced from the owner's $250). PROOF by day 10: at least 4 full $1,500 payments, a designer quote at or below $600 payable on delivery, and Stripe showing the first payout on or before day 17 -> plan 4 builds ordered day 10, delivered day 17, designers paid from the settled payments, about $3,303 net ($6,000 - $2,400 - $175 Stripe - $122) settled by day 21. STOP: fewer than 4 paid orders by day 10, no designer accepting pay-on-delivery at or below $600, or a first payout scheduled after day 17 -> stop at $122 spent; any order already paid is still built and delivered from its own payment. No CONTINUE batch: the window leaves no time for a second round.
